newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast light crudes slide with WTI.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast light crudes slide with WTI.

text.p: Late prices for U.S. West Coast crudes pared early losses but differentials for Alaskan crude stagnated with little change in the supply/demand picture.
Alaska North Slope's (ANS) diff stayed $2.30 a barrel under December cash West Texas Intermediate, the same level as the last deal done late in September.
Buyers said they kept bids at a $2.50 discount, while producers held offers at $2.10.
Refiners said ample crude supply and weak pump prices made current offers unattractive.

The American Petroleum Institute (API) showed on Tuesday that West Coast refiners saw large builds in crude oil stored at their facilities. The region's supply grew by 3.6 million barrels last week, according to data from the API.
Meanwhile, current refinery margins remained 21 percent weaker than last quarter.
Outright ANS prices rose with benchmark West Texas Intermediate (WTI). ending $20.20/$20.50, 15 cents lower than Monday.
On Tuesday, Line 63 also rose with WTI to $19.40/19.70 a barrel.
Wilmington remained at $18.15/$18.25 a barrel, while Kern River crude stayed $16.65/$16.85 a barrel.
